title: Contains Duplicate (Code War Chain)
inputFormat:
Line 1: integer n, the number of elements.
Line 2: n space-separated integers, the array nums.
outputFormat: A single integer, as described by the current stage.

examples.explanation: 2 appears twice, so a duplicate exists.

stages.title: Stage 1 - Contains Duplicate
stages.statement:
Given an array of `n` integers, print `1` if any value appears at least twice in the array, otherwise print `0`.

This is the warm-up stage of the chain — a plain existence check.

stages.title: Stage 2 - Find the Duplicate Index
stages.statement:
Enhancement of Stage 1: instead of just saying whether a duplicate exists, print the **0-based index** of the first element that duplicates a value seen earlier in the array. If no duplicate exists, print `-1`.

Your solution must run in **O(n)** time using a hash set/map — an O(n^2) brute-force comparison of every pair will time out once `n` grows large.

stages.title: Stage 3 - Count Distinct Duplicated Values
stages.statement:
Enhancement of Stage 2: print how many **distinct values** appear two or more times in the array (not the total count of repeated elements — count each duplicated value once).

Still solvable in **O(n)** with a frequency map.

stages.title: Stage 4 - Most Frequent Value
stages.statement:
Enhancement of Stage 3: print the value that occurs **most often** in the array. If several values tie for the highest frequency, print the **smallest** such value.

Still **O(n)**: one pass to build a frequency map, one pass to find the best value.

stages.title: Stage 5 - List All Duplicate Values
stages.statement:
Enhancement of Stage 4: print **every distinct value** that appears two or more times, sorted in ascending order, space-separated on one line. If there are none, print an empty line.

Building the frequency map is still O(n), but sorting the result pushes the expected complexity to **O(n log n)**.

stages.title: Stage 6 - Duplicate Within a Window of 3
stages.statement:
Enhancement of Stage 1: print `1` if there exist two **equal** values whose indices are at most **3 apart** (`|i - j| <= 3`), otherwise print `0`.

A sliding window of the last 3 values (a small hash set you add to / evict from as you scan) keeps this at **O(n)** — checking every pair within range for every index is O(n) per index and O(n^2) overall.

stages.title: Stage 7 - Longest Subarray Without Duplicates
stages.statement:
Final enhancement: print the length of the **longest contiguous subarray** that contains no duplicate values.

This is the hardest stage of the chain. A brute-force check of every subarray is O(n^2)/O(n^3). The optimal solution uses a **sliding window** with a hash map of last-seen indices to stay at **O(n)**.
